summary: The Superintendent of Public Instruction is a nonpartisan office that heads the state Department of Education, though CalMatters reports that starting in 2027 a governor-appointed education commissioner will run the department and many of the superintendent's duties move to the State Board of Education. The seat is open: Tony Thurmond is term-limited. Sonja Shaw, president of the Chino Valley Unified school board, placed first in the June 2 primary with 22.64%; Richard Barrera, president of the San Diego Unified school board, placed second with 20.30%. No party appears on the ballot, but Shaw is endorsed by the California Republican Party and Barrera by the California Teachers Association.

candidates.name: Sonja Shaw
candidates.party: Nonpartisan office (endorsed by the California Republican Party)

positions.stance: Back to basics in reading, writing, and math; cites that fewer than half of students read at grade level. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)

Opposes letting transgender girls use girls' locker rooms or play on girls' teams, and opposes protections for transgender students that she says bypass parental consent. (Ballotpedia candidate survey; CalMatters)
Led Chino Valley Unified's parental-notification fight, which drew a lawsuit from Attorney General Bonta; opposes pandemic-style closures and mandates. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)

candidates.name: Richard Barrera
candidates.party: Nonpartisan office (endorsed by the California Teachers Association)

positions.stance: Focuses on increasing school funding. (CalMatters voter guide)
Wants to expand early childhood education. (CalMatters)
Wants to make it easier to become a teacher. (CalMatters)

key_differences: Culture-war issues define Shaw's campaign, especially transgender student policy and parental notification; Barrera's campaign is about funding and staffing.
Coalitions: Shaw is backed by the state GOP, Moms for Liberty, and Steve Hilton; Barrera by the CTA and, unusually, by charter-school advocates as well.
Both are sitting school-board presidents, Shaw in Chino Valley and Barrera in San Diego Unified, the state's second-largest district.
The office itself is shrinking: the winner may hand day-to-day control of the Department of Education to an appointed commissioner starting in 2027.
